drug_class: Combination Diuretic (Water Pill) — Potassium-sparing diuretic plus Thiazide diuretic
purpose: This medication helps your body get rid of extra fluid and salt, which helps lower your blood pressure and reduce swelling in your legs or abdomen. It is commonly used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and a condition called edema where fluid builds up in the body. It can also be used for a hormonal condition called hyperaldosteronism where your body makes too much of a certain hormone.
how_it_works: Think of this as two water pills working together as a team. Hydrochlorothiazide tells your kidneys to flush out extra salt and water through your urine, which lowers fluid in your body and reduces blood pressure. Spironolactone blocks a hormone called aldosterone that normally tells your body to hold onto salt, and it also helps keep your potassium levels from dropping too low — something the other pill alone might cause. Together, they balance each other out nicely.
common_side_effects: You may feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when standing up quickly, so take it slow when getting up. You might urinate more often, particularly after your first dose. Some people notice muscle cramps, nausea, or an upset stomach. Men occasionally experience breast tenderness or enlargement. You may also feel more tired than usual.
warnings: Do not take this medication if your potassium levels are already too high, or if you have serious kidney problems. Because spironolactone keeps potassium in your body, avoid eating large amounts of potassium-rich foods like bananas or taking potassium supplements unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor right away if you notice an irregular heartbeat, muscle weakness, or extreme fatigue — these could be signs your potassium is too high. Avoid prolonged sun exposure as hydrochlorothiazide can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The most common starting dose is one tablet taken once or twice a day, usually in the morning with food to avoid an upset stomach. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how you respond and how your kidneys and potassium levels look on blood tests. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep it in your routine, and avoid taking it late in the evening so extra bathroom trips do not disturb your sleep.
